review: The whole hymn is Psalm 23 unfolded: 2:1–3 is v.1–2 (יְהוָה רֹעִי לֹא אֶחְסָר), 3:1–2 is v.3 (יְשֹׁבֵב נַפְשִׁי), 4:3 is v.4 (לֹא־אִירָא רָע), 5:1–2 is v.6 (אַךְ טוֹב וָחֶסֶד יִרְדְּפוּנִי). The psalm's own verbs are kept wherever the Arabic has a matching verb.
1:1 keeps the apposition יֵשׁוּעַ … רֹעִי as the Arabic يَسُوعُ رَبِّي رَاعِيَّ does, since the hymn's whole argument is that the Shepherd has a name.
2:5–6 keeps the possessive doubling of the Arabic (كُلُّ سَيِّدِي لِيَ … وَلِي خَيْرَاتُ نِعْمَتِهِ), so 'all my Master is mine' and 'the good of His grace is mine' stay two claims rather than one.
The two closing lines of every stanza are the 'how … how sweet' acclamation; stanza 5 repeats the sweet line twice in the print, and the payload does the same instead of adding a new adjective.

4:6 חֶלְקִי וְאֵין שֵׁנִי — the Arabic نَصِيبِي لَيْسَ لِي ثَان is 'my portion, I have no second'; the Hebrew keeps the sense of a second portion, not a second lord, which is why it is not rendered 'אין לי עוד אדון'.
